entries.reason: v5 has no URL routing: reload and Back always return to the Overview and the page title never changes. In ClearCase every view and document is a real route with its own history entry, filters live in the URL, and the title names the document, section and case. Evidence: src/lib/components/PageHeader.svelte:8.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 CSV export leaves formula prefixes unneutralised and a bare carriage return unquoted. ClearCase quotes cells containing a carriage return, and neutralises every exported text cell, imported or typed, at its start (also behind leading spaces, which a "Trim spaces" import removes) and after separators. A plain decimal number such as -5 and a validated signed-money amount keep their sign, so a spreadsheet reads a number; -1+2 and +27 phone numbers are neutralised. Evidence: src/lib/components/csv.ts:13.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 global search sets only the query and keeps stale Advanced Search filters, so it can return filtered or empty results. ClearCase has no separate global search box: search runs only through the Advanced Search form, whose filters are exactly those in its address, so no stale filter applies (as S-search-2). Evidence: src/lib/views/evidence/search.ts:18.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 has no URL routing, so reload, Back and a deep link always land on the Overview. In ClearCase each navigation entry is a real link to its own route, so reload, Back and deep links return to the same view, and the current view is marked for navigation. entries.reason: v5 toCSV does not quote a cell with a bare carriage return and does not neutralise formula prefixes, so imported or user-typed text can become a spreadsheet formula. ClearCase quotes cells with a carriage return, line feed, tab or semicolon, and every CSV export neutralises imported and user-typed text at its start (also behind leading spaces) and after any separator; only a plain decimal number and a validated signed-money amount keep a leading minus.
